title: Annual Update on the MMDVM Project
description: MMDVM hardware and software is at the core of most digital mode hotspots on the market. This talk is the annual update on the project. There is a lot new over the last year.

title: Rethinking Amateur Radio Emergency Services
description:
Bruce Perens K6BP will discuss a number of innovations for Amateur Radio Emergency Services. One is a new system for
emergency communications, employing multiple workstations per radio to
facilitate more efficient exchange of Incident Management
communications, and a novel method of computer route determination
that can steward the relaying of messages through multiple stations
across the country, or around the world, entirely by radio.

Bruce has also created an AI-based system that has turned the boring
PowerPoints of FEMA into exciting novels! They are made with story
development methods taken from Pixar, and incorporate interactive
memory-reinforcing Q&A, including reading and understanding ICS forms
that match the activity, throughout the story. While not yet
FEMA-approved, this training program makes it a breeze to learn the
material and, if necessary, pass the FEMA-mandated course.
-

title: Remote Operation of Your Ham Radio Station
description: Remote operation can make your station available at the places and times when you want to use it. If you cannot have a "home" station, remote operation will allow you to get on the air from other stations. We will cover the successful methods being used, help you avoid problems, and answer your questions.

title: Pico Balloon WSPR Tracker and LoRa APRS
description: A two-part talk on amateur-radio position tracking. The first half covers Kazu's custom RP2040-based pico balloon trackers — tiny solar-powered payloads transmitting WSPR on 20m and APRS on 2m, with launches that have circumnavigated the globe many times over (one flight logged 16+ trips around). The second half turns to LoRa APRS trackers and digipeaters built around the STM32WLE5, including ultra-low-power Channel Activity Detection modes that stretch two AA cells into months of digipeater operation — making remote, solar-powered, and battery-only sites genuinely practical.

title: PSKReporter – Past, Present and Future.
description: PSKReporter, introduced by Philip Gladstone (N1DQ), answers the core ham radio question: "Where am I being heard?". Since its 2008 inception, it has evolved into a central hub aggregating reception reports from thousands of worldwide ham operators using digital mode software like WSJT-X. The system processes UDP packets to provide real-time propagation data via map visualization. This talk will describe the path from the beginnings of Pskreporter in N1DQ’s basement, through the huge growth in digital mode traffic over the last 18 years to the present. It will conclude with a roadmap for the future and potential avenues to securing the future of the Pskreporter system.

title: Winlink Gateway Post Office Mode
description: Information on the January 2026 release of Winlink Post Office Mode how it works and the added features it provides.

title: EZ Printed Circuit Designs for QRP
description: QRPers are often active kit builders, but with the availability of free CAD tools and low-cost, low-volume printed circuit board fabricators, it is very easy to realize your own circuit design ideas or even just adapt someone else's circuit design, but with your own custom changes.  This talk will walk through the CAD tools, design, layout, and fabrication processes, using a simple QRP accessory as an example.

title: Venture Crew 73/ARISS
description: I've been an amateur radio operator for 20 years. I have taught the Technician Licensing class, 20 years. I have facilitated two ARISS contacts. I teach the Scouting America Radio and Electronica Merit Badge courses. As well as STEM programs.

title: SF Bay Area Skywarn
description:
*** This presentation will be an update to the one given at Pacificon 2025. ***

The National Weather Service (NWS) and Amateur Radio have both been around for over 100 years. SKYWARN is a volunteer program that is a joint collaboration between the NWS and a large number of trained weather spotters, many of whom are Amateur Radio operators. The role of SKYWARN volunteers involves providing assistance before, during, and after significant weather-related events. The SF Bay Area has had a SKYWARN program over many years. Since early 2024, this program has been re-invigorated and re-imagined. The current Bay Area SKYWARN program now has more tailored weather spotter training material in order to better serve the NWS staff and forecasters, given the unique nature and types of severe weather events that occur in our area. The program also has a website (sfoskywarn.org) that is used for disseminating the latest information about near-term storms, weather-related alerts, and weather spotter activation notices. Also, new techniques are being developed for submitting weather spotter reports. Of course, Amateur Radio continues to play a vital role in SKYWARN communications, particularly "when all else fails". This talk will give an overview of the SF Bay Area SKYWARN program and team. It will consist of a live presentation (slides) by Curt Kolovson W6RQ (SF Bay Area SKYWARN Volunteer Facilitator), some training material (slides and/or video produced by the NWS), and a speaker from the NWS Forecast Office in Monterey, CA (MTR), Brayden Murdock (Meteorologist and Skywarn Program Lead). The MTR office's coverage area includes 11 Bay Area counties of over 8 million people. Their office is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days per year.

title: Why Contesting?
description: Contesting is where great operators are made. It pushes you to master operating skills, build efficient stations, and understand propagation in real time. If you’re into emergency communications, contesting sharpens speed, accuracy, and decision-making under pressure. You’ll develop stamina, handle relentless pile-ups, and learn to adapt instantly. It’s also a playground for strategy—optimizing antennas, timing, and tactics for maximum results. No other aspect of amateur radio blends technical knowledge, operating excellence, and competitive spirit quite like contesting. If you want to elevate your skills and truly test your station, contesting is the ultimate arena.

title: Watch Duty: Behind the Scenes
description: An insider look into how Watch Duty operates.

title: Multi-State Auxiliary Communication Exercise panel discussion
description: The BEACON Exercise is a nationwide emergency communications exercise designed to test and strengthen community-based disaster response networks. Conducted annually, BEACON challenges volunteers, public safety partners, and community organizations to simulate real-world communication failures during large-scale disasters. Participants practice situational awareness reporting, message handling, and coordination across jurisdictions using resilient, independent communication methods. This panel will discuss how BEACON was developed, highlight lessons learned from 2026 and past exercises, and explore how communities can apply those insights locally. Audience will also have the opportunity to share their experiences, ask questions, and discuss ideas to improve the exercise for 2027.

title: Digital Amateur Television
description: We have been slowly updating systems in several locations to include digital output so part of this presentation will be an update. We are also looking at expanding services and capabilities onto multiple bands simultaneously and so the challenge is getting enough equipment stood up to support those new bands of service. And we are looking at turning on services way up into the 10 GHz microwave bands and also receiving signals from off planet when the time arrives.

title: Boats on the Air: Activating in a Marine Environment
description: Boats on the Air combines two passions, boating and ham radio, for twice the fun! This presentation will discuss the ins and outs of activating in a marine environment including antenna ideas, best practices, and special considerations while boating. Attendees will walk away with knowledge of how to successfully activate a ham radio station on any water-borne vessel.

title: Using WSPR to find Band Openings
description: WSPR, coupled with a multiband such as an end-fed half wave, can constantly scan the bands to tell you what is open to where. The presentation digs a little into WSPR technology and gives lots of examples.

title: Pacific Gaslighting & Interference: A QRM DF Adventure
description: Is powerline noise burying your HF signals? This is the story of two years spent chasing QRM - my ongoing adventures with our friends at PG&E. I'll share the direction-finding techniques I've picked up along the way, and the equally important off-air skills: keeping meticulous logs, engaging the ARRL, filing effective complaints, and using thorough documentation and sheer persistence to keep the pressure on a creatively evasive utility company.

title: Breaking Ohm's Law
description: Is Ohm’s Law really a law?  How about other laws, like Kirchhoff’s Laws for voltage and current, Lenz’s Law, and Snell’s Law?  In some cases these are reliable models that we can depend on, but in other cases they break down in some circumstances and can lead us astray.  Let’s take some time to learn about some of these so-called Laws and see how well they hold up under all sorts of circumstances.  And we will, of course, show how to break Ohm’s Law!

title: YLRL Forum (Part 1)
description: Come meet up with other YLs who enjoy your passion for Amateur Radio.  There will be a few short presentations, after which there will be time to share your stories and connect with others who share an interest in the areas you find most interesting in our hobby.

title: Modern Morse and AI: The DitStorm Cypher™ Story
description: Morse Nexus has been working on the development of breakthrough technology for CW operations. The initial releases of the Ditstorm Cypher are only the beginning of the story. AI has played a major role in helping push the technology forward, but it is also not the most important piece. We will present how the development took place, and what is the final goal, and where we are on the path to that goal with current Release 3.1

title: Using Spy Radios from WWII and the Cold War
description: Historical background of spy radio development, difference between spy radios and ordinary radios and how spy radios were used will be discussed. Four actual spy radios (B2, Paraset, GRC-109 and RS-6) will be shown. How to replicate the Paraset will also be presented.

title: The State of AREDN in 2026
description: Come and find out the latest from the AREDN amateur mesh networking world. We'll discuss the current state of AREDN, what's been happening, and what to expect in the future.

title: YLRL Forum (Part 2)
description: Come meet up with other YLs who enjoy your passion for Amateur Radio.  There will be a few short presentations, after which there will be time to share your stories and connect with others who share an interest in the areas you find most interesting in our hobby.

title: Engaging the Next Generation of Radio Amateurs
description: ARRL’s mission includes developing the next generation of radio amateurs. Learn about the programs, resources, and opportunities that are introducing young people to amateur radio, inspiring them to be active hams, and encouraging them to pursue higher education and careers in wireless technology and radio communications. Sponsored by ARRL The National Association for Amateur Radio®.

title: 3D Printing for Radio
description: A look at the world of 3D printing and the many useful things we can make for Amateur Radio.  Ill cover the different types of 3D printers and the different materials we can work with to make parts, antennas, cases, and other useful items.

title: Introduction to Microcontrollers
description: Join ARRL author Glen Popiel, KW5GP,  as he discusses the Arduino and other microcontrollers. Learn just how much fun you can have creating your own microcontroller-based projects for your ham shack, family, and friends.

title: Digital Library of Amateur Radio and Communications update
description: DLARC is Internet Archive's free online ham radio library, offering free access to callbooks, ham radio newsletters and magazines from around the world, conference archives, historical research, and more. The curator will show some of the material that has been added to the library in the past year, and what's next.

title: Trolling the International Space Station
description: history of Ameture radio on ISS, The antennas the Radios, What you can do to Work it!

title: A Novel Approach to CW Decode
description: Decoding noisy, ham-keyed CW isn't easy. Skilled humans still outperform every decoder in adverse conditions. We'll dig into what makes CW so challenging, explore current approaches, and put a statistical model to the test against seasoned ops.

title: Riding the Airwaves: Shortwave Listening in the 21st Century
description:
Pirates, spies, military coupes, opera singers, preachers, tech nerds, propaganda ministers, and artisans are all hanging out on the International Shortwave bands. Learn about Radio Caroline, the Japanese Slot Machine, the Numbers Stations, the Chinese Robot, the Russian Woodpecker, Radio Shoestring and more.

We will explore what can be heard on these bands today, touch on memorable stations of days gone by, learn how to set up your listening post, how to QSL, find clubs/resources, and much more.

BONUS: At the end of the session two lucky attendees will win a $200 ETON Elite Shortwave/AM/FM/VHF radio.

title: What's New With FreeDV
description: FreeDV has received a lot of audio quality and other improvements over the past few years, but did you know that it could get even better? In this talk, Mooneer K6AQ will talk about the next version of FreeDV's RADE mode and how it improves over the original version.

title: Analysis of FM Bandpass Filters for SOTA operations
description: We will present analysis of 2m bandpass filters both home made and commercial to mitigate interference and front end overload on summits with broadcast towers.  We will show both bench and field measurements and report on real-world performance.  We will also detail helical filter builds and tuning possibilities for some of the most challenging near-band interferences.

title: Advanced Antenna Measurement
description: This is a fully live and educational on-stage presentation. It shows how radio amateurs can use some professional VNA specific techniques to achieve highly accurate antenna measurements.

title: A Low Loss HF 1:2 Transmission Line Balun and Tutorial
description: A novel 1:2 impedance ratio balun is described that comprises the functions of a 1:4 impedance ratio Ruthroff balun and a 2:1 transformer built onto a single FT-240-43 toroid. The presentation includes a brief tutorial on transmission line baluns, followed by a description of the balun's operation, measured test results, and construction details. The balun covers 1.8 - 29.7 MHz with small signal insertion loss of 0.15 dB (96.6% efficiency), VSWR is less than 1.5:1, common mode rejection ratio (CMRR) of 26 - 18 dB, and impedance ratio can vary from about 1.6 to 2.8.

title: Dipole Impedance, Resonant Length, and Resonant Resistance
description: Popular antenna modeling programs do many things well but do some things poorly, even things that are simple and basic.  Perhaps most surprising, numerical programs do not predict a dipole's resonant frequency or resistance accurately.  We explore this problem from the perspective of antenna theory, and give simple formulas and graphs that are easy to use.  This talk expands on "The Mysterious Multiplying Factor K" which the author presented at Pacificon 2018.

title: End Fed Antenna Surprises
description:
You’ve got the transformer, and a roll of wire. How can this thing be set up?  Where’s the RF going to go?  What happens when you change bands?
Michelle will discuss the basics of this popular antenna, and show how the physics of this simple radiator can produce shocking surprises and very non-intuitive results.  Learn how this antenna behaves across the HF spectrum and how to take advantage of it’s characteristics.
